items.prompt: The medians of △ABC meet at the centroid G. The median from A has length 18. What is the distance from A to G?

wrong.why: Treated the centroid as the midpoint of the median.
Measured from the side instead of from the vertex (the short 1:2 part).
Used 3/4 of the median instead of 2/3.

items.explanation: The centroid divides each median 2:1, with the longer part at the vertex, so AG = (2/3)(18) = 12.

items.prompt: Three villages sit at the vertices of a scalene triangle. A well is to be the same distance from all three villages. Where should it be placed?
items.answer: At the meeting point of the perpendicular bisectors

wrong.text: At the meeting point of the three angle bisectors
wrong.why: That point (the incenter) is equidistant from the sides, not from the vertices.

wrong.text: At the meeting point of the three medians
wrong.why: That point (the centroid) is the balance point; it is not equidistant from the vertices of a scalene triangle.

wrong.text: At the meeting point of the three altitudes
wrong.why: The orthocenter is not equidistant from the vertices of a scalene triangle.

items.explanation: A point equidistant from two endpoints lies on their perpendicular bisector, so the circumcenter, where the three perpendicular bisectors meet, is equidistant from all three vertices.

items.prompt: A triangle has vertices (2, 3), (8, 3) and (5, 15). What is the y-coordinate of its centroid?
items.explanation: The centroid is the average of the vertices: y = (3 + 3 + 15) ÷ 3 = 7.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8 and hypotenuse 10. A circle is inscribed in it, tangent to all three sides, with its center at the incenter. What is the radius of that circle?

wrong.why: Gave the diameter of the inscribed circle.
Gave the circumradius (half the hypotenuse) instead of the inradius.
Halved the altitude to the hypotenuse (4.8 ÷ 2) instead of using area ÷ semiperimeter.

items.explanation: Area = 24 and semiperimeter = 12, so r = 24 ÷ 12 = 2. (Equivalently r = (6 + 8 − 10)/2.)

items.prompt: A triangle has vertices (0, 0), (8, 0) and (0, 6). Which point is its circumcenter?

wrong.why: This is the centroid, the average of the vertices.
This is the incenter (inradius 2), not the circumcenter.
Used only the perpendicular bisector of the horizontal leg and ignored the other.

items.explanation: The triangle is right-angled at the origin, so the circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse: ((8+0)/2, (0+6)/2) = (4, 3), which is 5 from each vertex.

items.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 3x + 2 and CD = 5x − 6. What is the length of AB?

wrong.why: Reported the value of x instead of the length.
Used 3x without adding the 2.
Used 5x as the length, dropping the 6.

items.explanation: Opposite sides are congruent: 3x + 2 = 5x − 6, so x = 4 and AB = 3(4) + 2 = 14.

items.prompt: The diagonals of parallelogram ABCD meet at E. AE = 2y + 3 and EC = 4y − 9. What is the length of diagonal AC?

wrong.why: Gave AE only, half the diagonal.
Added 2y and 4y but ignored the constants (6y with y = 6).
Used 4y only, with y = 6.

items.explanation: Diagonals bisect each other, so 2y + 3 = 4y − 9 and y = 6. Then AE = 15 and AC = 2 · 15 = 30.

items.prompt: To prove that the diagonals of parallelogram ABCD bisect each other, the diagonals meet at E and you show △ABE ≅ △CDE. Using AB ∥ CD, you know ∠BAE ≅ ∠DCE and ∠ABE ≅ ∠CDE (alternate interior angles), and AB = CD (opposite sides). Which congruence criterion finishes the step?
items.answer: ASA, using two angle pairs and the side between them

wrong.text: SAS, using two side pairs and the angle between them
wrong.why: Only one pair of sides (AB and CD) is known to be congruent, so SAS cannot be used.

wrong.text: SSS, using all three pairs of sides
wrong.why: Only AB = CD is known; AE = CE and BE = DE is what you are trying to prove.

wrong.text: HL, using a hypotenuse and a leg pair
wrong.why: Nothing says the triangles have a right angle.

items.explanation: Two pairs of congruent angles plus the congruent side between them (AB and CD) give ASA, so AE = CE and BE = DE by CPCTC.

items.prompt: In parallelogram PQRS the diagonals PR and QS are congruent. Which statement must be true?
items.answer: All four angles are right angles

wrong.why: A non-square rectangle has congruent diagonals but unequal adjacent sides.
A non-square rectangle has congruent diagonals that are not perpendicular.
A non-square rectangle has diagonals that do not bisect its angles.

items.explanation: A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle, so every angle is 90°. The other properties hold only for a rhombus or square.

items.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD has A(1, 1), B(6, 3) and C(10, 8), and is a parallelogram with vertices in that order. What is the x-coordinate of D?
items.explanation: The diagonals bisect each other, so the midpoints of AC and BD match: D = A + C − B = (1 + 10 − 6, 1 + 8 − 3) = (5, 6).

items.prompt: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm. What is the length of one side, in cm?
items.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so each side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 and 12: √(25 + 144) = 13.

items.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = (2x + 10)° and ∠B = (3x − 5)°. What is the measure of ∠B?

wrong.why: Gave ∠A instead of ∠B.
Gave the value of x.
Used 3x and forgot to subtract 5.

items.explanation: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: 5x + 5 = 180, so x = 35 and ∠B = 3(35) − 5 = 100°.

items.prompt: In △ABC, M and N are the midpoints of AB and AC. MN = x + 5 and BC = 4x − 6. What is BC?

wrong.why: Gave MN, half of BC.
Gave the value of x.
Doubled BC a second time.

items.explanation: The midsegment is half the third side: x + 5 = (4x − 6)/2, so x = 8 and BC = 26.

items.prompt: A quadrilateral's diagonals bisect each other. They are not congruent and they are not perpendicular. Which is the most specific name guaranteed for the quadrilateral?

wrong.why: Rectangles have congruent diagonals.
Rhombuses have perpendicular diagonals.
Kites have perpendicular diagonals.

items.explanation: Diagonals that bisect each other make it a parallelogram. Non-congruent diagonals rule out a rectangle, and non-perpendicular diagonals rule out a rhombus or kite.

items.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD has A(0, 0), B(4, 3), C(9, 3) and D(5, 0). Which description is fully justified by the coordinates?
items.answer: A rhombus that is not a rectangle

wrong.text: A rectangle that is not a square
wrong.why: Adjacent sides AB (slope 3/4) and AD (slope 0) are not perpendicular.
The angles are not right angles.

wrong.text: A parallelogram with no two adjacent sides congruent
wrong.why: All four sides have length 5, so adjacent sides are congruent.

items.explanation: AB ∥ DC (slope 3/4) and AD ∥ BC (slope 0), and AB = BC = CD = DA = 5, so it is a rhombus. AB and AD are not perpendicular, so it is not a rectangle.

items.prompt: In a circle, a central angle measures 110°. An inscribed angle intercepts the same arc. What is the measure of the inscribed angle?

wrong.why: Took the inscribed angle equal to the central angle.
Doubled the central angle.
Used the supplement of 110°.

items.explanation: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc, and the arc equals the central angle: 110° ÷ 2 = 55°.

items.prompt: Point P is outside a circle with center O and radius 5. PT is tangent to the circle at T, and OP = 13. What is PT?

wrong.why: Subtracted the radius from OP (13 − 5).
Added the radius to OP (13 + 5).
Added the squares (√(13² + 5²) ≈ 13.9) instead of subtracting.

items.explanation: The radius OT is perpendicular to the tangent PT, so △OTP is a right triangle with hypotenuse 13: PT = √(13² − 5²) = 12.

items.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle with ∠A = (2x + 14)° and ∠C = (4x − 2)°. What is the measure of ∠C?

wrong.why: Gave ∠A instead of ∠C.
Set ∠A = ∠C instead of making them supplementary.
Gave the value of x.

items.explanation: Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary: 6x + 12 = 180, so x = 28 and ∠C = 4(28) − 2 = 110°.

items.prompt: Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at E. AE = 6, EB = 8 and CE = 4. What is ED?
items.explanation: Chord segments satisfy AE · EB = CE · ED, so 48 = 4 · ED and ED = 12.

items.prompt: From external point P, tangent segment PT has length 6. A secant from P meets the circle at A (nearer) and B (farther), with PA = 4. What is the length of chord AB?

wrong.why: Gave the whole secant PB instead of the chord AB.
Subtracted the tangent and the external segment (6 − 4).
Added the tangent and the external segment (6 + 4).

items.explanation: Tangent–secant: PT² = PA · PB, so 36 = 4 · PB and PB = 9. Then AB = 9 − 4 = 5.

items.prompt: Two secants meet at a point outside a circle. They intercept a far arc of 100° and a near arc of 30°. What is the measure of the angle they form?

wrong.why: Averaged the arcs (added them and halved) instead of finding half the difference.
Took the full difference without halving.
Added the arcs.

items.explanation: An angle formed outside by two secants is half the difference of the intercepted arcs: (100° − 30°) ÷ 2 = 35°.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 9. A central angle of 40° intercepts an arc. What is the arc length?

wrong.why: Used the diameter 18 as the radius.
Gave the full circumference.
Multiplied 9 × 40 using degrees as if they were radians.

items.prompt: A sector has radius 10 and a central angle of π/5 radians. What is the area of the sector?

wrong.why: Used r²θ and forgot the factor 1/2.
Found the arc length rθ instead of the area.
Used the diameter 20 as the radius.

items.prompt: Two concentric circles have radii 6 and 15. A central angle of 60° intercepts an arc of length 2π on the smaller circle. What is the length of the arc the same angle intercepts on the larger circle?

wrong.why: Inverted the ratio, using 6/15 instead of 15/6.
Squared the ratio of radii (as for area).
Added the difference in radii instead of scaling.

items.explanation: Arc length is proportional to radius for a fixed angle: (15/6)(2π) = 5π.

items.prompt: A runner jogs along a circular track of radius 30 m. The arc covers a central angle of 1.2 radians. How far does the runner go, in meters?
A sector of a circle has radius 18 and an arc length of 12π. What is the area of the sector?

wrong.why: Used r · s without the factor 1/2.
Gave the area of the entire circle.
Halved the correct area twice.

items.prompt: Which is the equation of the circle with center (−3, 2) and radius 4?

wrong.why: Sign slips: used (3, −2) as the center.
Used r instead of r² on the right.
Doubled the radius instead of squaring it.

items.explanation: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² with h = −3, k = 2, r² = 16.

items.prompt: A circle has equation x² + y² + 8x − 6y + 9 = 0. What are its center and radius?

wrong.why: Sign slips in the center.
Gave r² as the radius.
Ignored the constant +9 when finishing the square.

items.prompt: The circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0 has a radius of what length?
items.explanation: Complete the square: (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 12 + 9 + 4 = 25, so r = 5.

items.prompt: A circle has center (2, −1) and passes through (5, 3). Which is its equation?

wrong.why: Wrote the radius 5 instead of r² = 25.
Sign slips in the center.
Added the leg lengths 3 + 4 = 7 and squared, instead of using the Pythagorean theorem.

items.explanation: r² = (5 − 2)² + (3 − (−1))² = 9 + 16 = 25, by the Pythagorean theorem.

items.prompt: A cone has radius 6 and height 10. What is its volume?

wrong.why: Forgot the factor 1/3.
Used the diameter 12 as the radius.
Used r instead of r² in the formula.

items.prompt: A sphere has radius 6. What is its volume?

wrong.why: Gave the surface area 4πr².
Used 4πr³ and dropped the 1/3.
Used r² instead of r³.

items.prompt: A square pyramid has a base side of 8 and a volume of 128. What is its height?
A solid is a cylinder of radius 4 and height 10 with a hemisphere of radius 4 attached to one circular end. What is its total volume?

wrong.why: Used a full sphere instead of a hemisphere.
Left out the hemisphere.
Used 2πr³ for the hemisphere instead of (2/3)πr³.

items.explanation: Cylinder: π(16)(10) = 160π. Hemisphere: (2/3)π(64) = 128π/3. Total = 608π/3.

items.prompt: The radius of a cylinder is tripled and its height is cut in half. By what factor does the volume change?

wrong.why: Treated both changes as linear (3 × 1/2).
Squared the radius change but ignored the height.
Doubled the height instead of halving it.

items.explanation: V = πr²h scales by 3² × 1/2 = 9/2.

items.prompt: A plane cuts a cone parallel to its circular base, not through the apex. What is the shape of the cross-section?

wrong.why: That needs a slanted plane that cuts the base and does not run parallel to it.
That needs a plane through the apex.
That needs a plane parallel to a slant line of the cone.

items.explanation: Every parallel slice of a cone is a smaller circle.

items.prompt: A right triangle with legs 3 and 4 is rotated about its leg of length 4. What solid is formed?
items.answer: A cone with radius 3 and height 4

wrong.text: A cone with radius 4 and height 3
wrong.why: Swapped the axis and the radius.

wrong.text: A cylinder with radius 3 and height 4
wrong.why: Rotating a triangle gives a cone, not a cylinder.

wrong.text: A cone with radius 5 and height 4
wrong.why: Used the hypotenuse as the radius.

items.explanation: The leg on the axis is the height (4); the other leg sweeps out the base, radius 3.

items.prompt: The rectangle with vertices (1, 0), (3, 0), (3, 5) and (1, 5) is rotated about the y-axis. What solid results?
items.answer: A cylinder of radius 3 with a hole of radius 1

wrong.text: A solid cylinder of radius 3 and height 5
wrong.why: Ignored the gap between the rectangle and the axis.

wrong.text: A solid cylinder of radius 2 and height 5
wrong.why: Used the width of the rectangle as the radius.

wrong.text: A cone with base radius 3 and height 5
wrong.why: Rotating a rectangle cannot produce a cone.

items.explanation: The edge at x = 1 sweeps a hole of radius 1 and the edge at x = 3 the outer wall of radius 3, over a height of 5.

items.prompt: A plane through the center of a cube is perpendicular to the diagonal joining two opposite vertices. What is the shape of the cross-section?

wrong.why: That arises from a plane cutting off a single corner.
That arises from a plane parallel to a face.

wrong.text: A rectangle that is not a square
wrong.why: That arises from a plane through two opposite edges.

items.explanation: The plane meets six faces at the midpoints of six edges, giving a regular hexagon.

items.prompt: A solid steel ball has radius 3 cm. Steel has density 7.8 g/cm³. To the nearest gram, what is the mass of the ball?
A concrete block is 2 m long, 0.5 m wide and 0.4 m thick. Concrete has density 2400 kg/m³. What is the mass of the block?

wrong.why: Divided the density by the volume.
Used only 2 × 0.5 and forgot the thickness.
Added the dimensions instead of multiplying.

items.prompt: A label covers only the curved side of a cylindrical can with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Label material costs $0.02 per cm². About how much does one label cost?

wrong.why: Included the top and bottom.
Used πrh and dropped the factor 2.
Used the volume instead of area.

items.prompt: An open-top box with a square base must hold 32 m³. To use the least material, which dimensions (base side × base side × height, in m) should be chosen from these options?

wrong.why: Needs 68 m² of material.
Needs 80 m² of material.
Needs 129 m² of material.

items.explanation: Material = base + four sides: 4×4×2 uses 16 + 32 = 48 m², less than 68, 80 or 129.

items.prompt: A model of a sculpture is built at a scale of 1:5 (every length is 1/5 of the real length). The model has a volume of 40 cm³. What is the real sculpture's volume, in cm³?
items.explanation: Volume scales with the cube of the scale factor: 40 × 5³ = 40 × 125 = 5000 cm³.

items.prompt: A rectangular town measures 3 miles by 1.5 miles and has 4500 residents. What is its population density?

wrong.why: Divided by 3 only.
Divided by 1.5 only.
Multiplied people by area.

items.explanation: Area = 4.5 mi²; density = 4500 ÷ 4.5 = 1000.
